title: Overlap distribution of the critical Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model
abstract: We study the distribution of the two-replica overlap $R_{1,2}$ in the Ising and spherical Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models at the critical inverse temperature $β= 1$. Our main result shows that in both models, $R_{1,2}$ has scale $N^{-1/3}$, and the quenched distribution of $N^{1/3} R_{1,2}$ converges to an explicit random probability measure defined in terms of the reflected $\mathrm{Airy}_1$ point process. As a consequence, we characterize the limiting value of $N^{2/3} \mathbb{E} \langle R_{1,2}^2 \rangle$, answering a question of Talagrand \cite{talagrand2011mean2}.   For the spherical SK model, we obtain the limit by representing the Gibbs measure as an anisotropic Gaussian on $\mathbb{R}^N$ conditioned to have norm $\sqrt{N}$, and then passing to the $\mathrm{Airy}_1$ scaling limit at the GOE spectral edge. For the Ising SK model, the proof is based on a sphere-to-cube comparison principle showing that the quenched distributions of $N^{1/3} R_{1,2}$ under the spherical and Ising Gibbs measures asymptotically coincide.   This paper is a companion to \cite{du2026fluctuations}, where we introduced a related comparison principle to identify the limiting fluctuations of the SK free energy. Most of the arguments in this paper were generated using GPT-5.6 Pro, with the aim of exploring further consequences of the ideas developed in that work.
summary: This paper rigorously determines the limiting distribution of the two-replica overlap for the critical Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass model. The key finding is that this distribution converges to a measure defined by the reflected Airy$_1$ point process. This work provides deep mathematical insights into disordered systems, connecting them to established results in random matrix theory.
main_problem: The study focuses on determining the distribution of the two-replica overlap ($R_{1,2}$) in the critical Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) model.
main_result: The quenched distribution of the scaled overlap converges to a random probability measure defined by the reflected Airy$_1$ point process for both Ising and spherical SK models at criticality ($ eta=1$).
method: The analysis employs advanced techniques including comparison principles (sphere-to-cube) and passing to scaling limits derived from Gaussian representations, connecting the problem to Random Matrix Theory.
model_or_system: The system is the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass model, analyzed in both its Ising and spherical variants. The Hamiltonian involves interactions defined by a random matrix $\mathbf{W}$, and the study centers on the Gibbs measure at the critical inverse temperature $ eta=1$.
key_observables: Two-replica overlap ($R_{1,2}$), quenched distribution of $N^{1/3} R_{1,2}$, and the expectation value $\mathbb{E} \langle R_{1,2}^2 angle$.
important_parameters: Critical inverse temperature ($ eta=1$), scaling factor $N^{-1/3}$, and convergence to the reflected Airy$_1$ point process.
main_assumptions: The derivation for the spherical model relies on representing the Gibbs measure as an anisotropic Gaussian conditioned on norm $\sqrt{N}$. The Ising case uses a comparison principle showing asymptotic coincidence with the spherical case.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the overlap distribution, first establishing general scaling laws and then deriving the specific limiting measure (reflected Airy$_1$ process) for both the spherical and Ising SK models by leveraging connections to Gaussian measures and random matrix theory.
why_interesting: While focused on spin glasses, the rigorous mathematical techniques involving convergence of point processes ($\mathrm{Airy}_1$) and scaling limits are highly relevant to understanding critical phenomena in complex quantum many-body systems where disorder is present.
